title: Paramārthacarcā — Discourse on the Ultimate
author: Ascribed to Abhinavagupta (transmitted in the Abhinavastotrāvali)
text:
The Paramārthacarcā is a hymn of eight verses ascribed to Abhinavagupta and transmitted with the collection of his stotras known as the Abhinavastotrāvali. Its meditation turns on a single inversion of ordinary seeing: distinct from every lit thing, light itself does not shine as an object — it is too pervasive to appear; and the division of the world into what illumines and what is illumined is a division made from within consciousness, not over it.

Its juice: the eight verses carry the Trika's epistemology in devotional form. The Ultimate discussed here is not elsewhere than the act of knowing — it is that act unobjectified. The poem's force is to leave the reader mid-sequence, hunting the lamp while standing in its light.
